pr_title: Warn the user if they're specifying protocols that won't be used
pr_body:
# Warn the user if they're specifying protocols that won't be used

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

Summary of the changes (Less than 80 chars)

## Description

If TLS is disabled and HTTP/1.x is available, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 will be disabled.  This is predictable for HTTP/3, which requires TLS, but may surprise users of HTTP/2 which can be used without TLS if HTTP/1.x is not available.
    
Fixes #43837

issue_context.title: Http1AndHttp2 should warn if Tls is disabled
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

When TLS is off and Http1AndHttp2 is set in protocol, the developer should be notified that Http/2 will be disabled.

### Expected Behavior

Possibly add a log warning in this section of code telling me that Http/2 was disabled because TLS was switched off, instead of having me run in circles trying to fix my SSL ALPN implementation.

See https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/KestrelServerImpl.cs:167

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

_No response_

_No response_

### Anything else?

_No response_
comments: Note we do not log a warning for this today because Http1AndHttp2 is the default setting, it would cause this warning in most apps on their non-TLS endpoints.

Seems reasonable/easy enough to add a Info-level log here: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/349ddc9b8bf8255166f87899d7905510f362a5d5/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/KestrelServerImpl.cs#L157-L163

Thanks for contacting us.

We're moving this issue to the `.NET 8 Planning` milestone for future evaluation / consideration. We would like to keep this around to collect more feedback, which can help us with prioritizing this work. We will re-evaluate this issue, during our next planning meeting(s). 
If we later determine, that the issue has no community involvement, or it's very rare and low-impact issue, we will close it - so that the team can focus on more important and high impact issues.
To learn more about what to expect next and how this issue will be handled you can read more about our triage process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/docs/TriageProcess.md).
We should only warn if the user has _specified_ HTTP/2 and TLS is off. We don't want the warning in the default case.
@amcasey Can you look into this one? @Tratcher can help get you up to speed.
Hey @arontsang, can you give me a little more context on why you closed this issue?  Is it working as expected now?

review_comments: I don't love these magic numbers (though they arguably can't change without breaking back-compat).  Would it be worthwhile to define constants?
This is tolerable since it's test code and the test will fail immediately if it ever changes.
